\section[prever]{prever — to foresee, to predict}

\label{lesson:PT-C371-prever}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for possible, then the Portuguese for possibly.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: prever}
\textbf{prever} — \textquotedblleft{}to foresee, to predict\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Ninguém previu tanta chuva.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Nobody predicted so much rain.}
\end{quote}

Conjugated like \emph{ver}: \emph{prevejo, prevês, prevê}. \emph{Estar previsto} — to be scheduled.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{prever} is built from \emph{pre-} \textquotedblleft{}before\textquotedblright{} and \emph{ver} \textquotedblleft{}to see\textquotedblright{}, modelled on Latin \emph{praevidēre} \textquotedblleft{}to foresee\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), on \emph{vidēre} \textquotedblleft{}to see\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{prever}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{prever}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{prever}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for possible, then the Portuguese for possibly, then say \emph{prever} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does prever mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To foresee, to predict\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[previsível]{previsível — predictable}

\label{lesson:PT-C371-previsivel}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for possibly, then the Portuguese for to foresee.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: previsível}
\textbf{previsível} — \textquotedblleft{}predictable\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
O final do filme era muito previsível.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The end of the film was very predictable.}
\end{quote}

Built on \emph{prever} + \emph{-ível}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{previsível} is built on \emph{previsto}, the participle of \emph{prever} \textquotedblleft{}to foresee\textquotedblright{}, with \emph{-ível}; the verb rests on Latin \emph{vidēre} \textquotedblleft{}to see\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{previsível}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{previsível}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{previsível}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for possibly, then the Portuguese for to foresee, then say \emph{previsível} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[imprevisível]{imprevisível — unpredictable}

\label{lesson:PT-C371-imprevisivel}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to foresee, then the Portuguese for predictable.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: imprevisível}
\textbf{imprevisível} — \textquotedblleft{}unpredictable\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
O tempo na montanha é imprevisível.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The weather in the mountains is unpredictable.}
\end{quote}

The opposite of \emph{previsível}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{imprevisível} is built from \emph{in-} \textquotedblleft{}not\textquotedblright{} and \emph{previsível} \textquotedblleft{}predictable\textquotedblright{}, on \emph{prever}, which rests on Latin \emph{vidēre} \textquotedblleft{}to see\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[o imprevisto]{o imprevisto — the unexpected problem, the hitch}

\label{lesson:PT-C371-imprevisto}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for predictable, then the Portuguese for unpredictable.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: o imprevisto}
\textbf{o imprevisto} — \textquotedblleft{}the unexpected problem, the hitch\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Tive um imprevisto e cheguei tarde.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Something unexpected came up and I arrived late.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Salvo imprevistos} — barring the unexpected.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{imprevisto} is built from \emph{in-} \textquotedblleft{}not\textquotedblright{} and \emph{previsto} \textquotedblleft{}foreseen\textquotedblright{}, the participle of \emph{prever}, on Latin \emph{vidēre} \textquotedblleft{}to see\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[a alternativa]{a alternativa — the alternative, the other option}

\label{lesson:PT-C371-alternativa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for unpredictable, then the Portuguese for the unexpected problem.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a alternativa}
\textbf{a alternativa} — \textquotedblleft{}the alternative, the other option\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Não temos alternativa: vamos de táxi.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{We have no alternative: we are going by taxi.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Em alternativa} — alternatively.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{alternativa} is built on \emph{alternativo} (EtymDB), from Medieval Latin \emph{alternātīvus}, on \emph{alternus} \textquotedblleft{}one after the other\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{alter} \textquotedblleft{}the other\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
